# keycard_provider (Resource)

Manages a Keycard provider. A provider is a system that supplies access to resources and allows actors (users or applications) to authenticate.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create a zone
resource "keycard_zone" "dev" {
  name = "Development"
}

# Register an OAuth2 identity provider
resource "keycard_provider" "okta" {
  zone_id       = keycard_zone.dev.id
  name          = "Okta"
  client_id     = var.okta_oauth_client_id
  client_secret = var.okta_oauth_client_secret

  oauth2 = {
    issuer = "https://dev-12345.okta.com"
  }
}

# Configure the zone to use Okta for user authentication
resource "keycard_zone_user_identity_config" "dev" {
  zone_id     = keycard_zone.dev.id
  provider_id = keycard_provider.okta.id
}
```

## Identifier and Issuer

A provider has two key fields:

- **`identifier`** — A unique key within the zone. Can be any string.
- **`oauth2.issuer`** — The OIDC issuer URL used for discovery and token validation.

There are three ways to configure them:

### Identifier only (backward compatible)

When `oauth2` is not set, the `identifier` is sent to the API as-is. The API
copies it into `protocols.oauth2.issuer` automatically. This is the original
behavior — existing configurations continue to work without changes.

```terraform
resource "keycard_provider" "okta" {
  zone_id       = keycard_zone.dev.id
  name          = "Okta"
  identifier    = "https://dev-12345.okta.com"
  client_id     = var.okta_client_id
  client_secret = var.okta_client_secret
}
```

### Explicit issuer (recommended for new configs)

Set `oauth2.issuer` to make the OIDC issuer explicit. When `identifier` is
omitted, it defaults to the `issuer` value.

```terraform
resource "keycard_provider" "okta" {
  zone_id       = keycard_zone.dev.id
  name          = "Okta"
  client_id     = var.okta_client_id
  client_secret = var.okta_client_secret

  oauth2 = {
    issuer = "https://dev-12345.okta.com"
  }
}
```

### Multiple providers with the same issuer

When multiple providers share the same OIDC issuer (e.g., separate OAuth clients
for marketing and engineering), set a custom `identifier` to keep them unique
within the zone:

```terraform
resource "keycard_provider" "acme_marketing" {
  zone_id       = keycard_zone.dev.id
  name          = "Acme Marketing"
  identifier    = "acme-marketing"
  client_id     = var.marketing_client_id
  client_secret = var.marketing_client_secret

  oauth2 = {
    issuer = "https://sso.acme.com/oauth2/default"
  }
}

resource "keycard_provider" "acme_engineering" {
  zone_id       = keycard_zone.dev.id
  name          = "Acme Engineering"
  identifier    = "acme-engineering"
  client_id     = var.engineering_client_id
  client_secret = var.engineering_client_secret

  oauth2 = {
    issuer = "https://sso.acme.com/oauth2/default"
  }
}
```

## Signing Keys

To verify tokens a provider issues, such as workload identity tokens, Keycard
needs the provider's signing keys. By default it finds them through OIDC
discovery on `oauth2.issuer`. Two settings change where the keys come from. You
can set one of them, not both.

### JWKS URI

Set `oauth2.jwks_uri` when the issuer publishes its keys but has no discovery
document, for example SPIFFE/SPIRE without the OIDC Discovery Provider.

```terraform
resource "keycard_provider" "spire" {
  zone_id = keycard_zone.dev.id
  name    = "SPIRE"

  oauth2 = {
    issuer   = "https://spire.example.com"
    jwks_uri = "https://spire.example.com/keys"
  }
}
```

### Static JWKS

Set `oauth2.jwks` when Keycard can't reach the issuer at all, for example a
local Kubernetes cluster or an air-gapped IdP. Keycard verifies tokens against
these keys and never contacts the issuer. The value is a JWK Set as a JSON
string, with 1 to 20 public RSA or EC keys, each with a unique `kid`.

```terraform
resource "keycard_provider" "local_cluster" {
  zone_id = keycard_zone.dev.id
  name    = "Local Kubernetes"

  oauth2 = {
    issuer = "https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local"
    # The output of `kubectl get --raw /openid/v1/jwks`
    jwks = file("${path.module}/cluster-jwks.json")
  }
}
```

Changes in whitespace or member order don't cause a diff. Keycard trusts the
keys until you remove them, so when the issuer rotates keys, add the new key
to the set before the issuer signs with it, and remove the old key afterward.

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable name for the provider.
- `zone_id` (String) The zone this provider belongs to. Changing this will replace the provider.

### Optional

- `client_id` (String) OAuth 2.0 client identifier.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) OAuth 2.0 client secret.
- `description` (String) Optional description of the provider's purpose.
- `identifier` (String) User-specified identifier, must be unique within the zone. Defaults to the `oauth2.issuer` value when not set.
- `oauth2` (Attributes) OAuth 2.0 protocol configuration. When provided, `issuer` is required. If `identifier` is not set, it defaults to the `issuer` value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--oauth2))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the provider.

<a id="nestedatt--oauth2"></a>
### Nested Schema for `oauth2`

Required:

- `issuer` (String) OIDC issuer URL used for discovery and token validation. Must be a valid URI.

Optional:

- `authorization_endpoint` (String) OAuth 2.0 Authorization endpoint URL.
- `jwks` (String) Static JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517), as a JSON string such as `jsonencode({ keys = [...] })` or `file("jwks.json")`. Keycard verifies the provider's tokens against these keys and never contacts the issuer, which suits local or air-gapped issuers Keycard can't reach. The set holds 1 to 20 public RSA or EC (P-256, P-384, P-521) keys, each with a unique `kid`. Keys stay trusted until removed, so add a rotated key before the issuer starts signing with it. Conflicts with `jwks_uri`. Removing it from the configuration clears it on the provider.
- `jwks_uri` (String) URL of the provider's JSON Web Key Set. When set, Keycard fetches signing keys from this URL instead of using OIDC discovery, which suits issuers without a discovery document, such as SPIFFE/SPIRE. Conflicts with `jwks`. Removing it from the configuration clears it on the provider.
- `token_endpoint` (String) OAuth 2.0 Token endpoint URL.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Providers can be imported using the format: zones/{zone-id}/providers/{provider-id}
import {
  to = keycard_provider.okta
  id = "zones/zone-id-123/providers/provider-id-xyz"
}

resource "keycard_provider" "okta" {
  # Configuration will be populated after import
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Providers can be imported using the format: zones/{zone-id}/providers/{provider-id}
terraform import keycard_provider.okta zones/zone-id-123/providers/provider-id-xyz
```
